messages:
maria_s: Quick sync — we're finalizing AWS KMS integration for Redwood Private (VPC). Control plane will live in customer's account; dataplane runs in our infra. Two quick asks: 1) recommended DEK caching window and grant model for cross-account decrypts, 2) audit log expectations for incident triage.
jonathan: For performance we cache DEKs in-memory on each dataplane worker for 2 minutes by default, with a hot-path fallback to rewrap via KMS if cache miss. That keeps KMS QPS manageable.
ashley: 2 minutes seems short for high-throughput customers. Can we make it configurable per-deployment? Also need a plan for revocation — how do we force immediate invalidation if CMK is compromised?
maria_s: Yes configurable. For revocation we rely on CMK disable/rotate + versioned DEK envelope tags. But disable alone won't revoke already-decrypted DEKs in memory. We need an orchestration step to push rotation signals to workers.
devops_tony: Suggest adding a key-rotation webhook: control plane writes rotation event to customer pubsub and dataplane subscribes; on receipt each worker zeroes DEK cache and fetches new encrypted DEK. Works for Private VPC where we have secure control channel.
sre_lee: For audits — CloudTrail records KMS:Encrypt/Decrypt and GenerateDataKey calls in the customer's account. We should also emit dataplane-level audit events (DEK-cache-hit/miss, key-id used) to our centralized audit stream so we can correlate.
ashley: We also need an IAM/grant example for the cross-account usage. Customers want least-privilege policy.
maria_s: Here's a minimal key policy we proposed:```{  "Version": "2012-10-17",  "Statement": [    {"Sid":"AllowControlPlaneRole",     "Effect":"Allow",     "Principal":{"AWS":"arn:aws:iam::CUSTOMER_ACCT:role/rp-controlplane-role"},     "Action":["kms:GenerateDataKey","kms:Encrypt","kms:Decrypt","kms:ReEncrypt*"],     "Resource":"*"    }  ]}```
jonathan: We'll also recommend creating ephemeral grants via kms:CreateGrant with Constraints: {"EncryptionContext:service":"redwood"} and a TTL of 300s so rolling workers can use grants without long-lived IAM wideness. Grants help avoid broad key policy changes.
sec-bot: Reminder: CloudTrail logs grants and CreateGrant events. But note CreateGrant does not log plaintext DEKs; that's only within KMS.
sre_lee: For incident response we should keep the following timeline items in our playbook: 1) detect suspicious API call pattern (abnormal GenerateDataKey), 2) verify CloudTrail in customer acct, 3) issue CMK disable/rotate if confirmed, 4) send rotation webhook and rotate DEK envelopes, 5) postmortem with access tree.
maria_s: One open question: are we comfortable storing encrypted DEKs in etcd inside customer VPC control plane? We currently plan to store AES-wrapped DEKs (KMS ciphertext) with metadata: key-id, version, created_by.
ashley: That's OK if etcd is in the customer's VPC and access is RBAC restricted. Add encryption-at-rest (EBS/GMS) and strict etcd ACLs. Also tag DEK objects with rotation epoch.
devops_tony: For rotation semantics: we will implement staged rollout — new DEK envelopes created, workers accept both old and new for a 24h overlap, then we garbage-collect old envelopes after confirmation. Helps avoid tears on long-running sessions.
jonathan: Edge case: cross-account grants expire mid-request. Add a short internal retry to re-request a fresh decrypt grant (CreateGrant) or fallback to customer-specified software key if allowed. We should surface that in SDK errors.
maria_s: Compliance question: do we need to preserve DEK usage events for 7 years? Some customers asked for long-term audit trails.
sre_lee: We can ship DEK usage telemetry (key-id, timestamp, action, resource-id) to customer-controlled S3 in their account; retention policy is customer-configurable. Avoid sending plaintext or DEK material.
ashley: Vulnerability triage note — if a worker image has RCE and an attacker can read process memory, cached DEKs could be exposed. Mitigations: mlock sensitive buffers, minimal caching TTL, and mandatory CMK rotation on suspicious host compromise.
maria_s: Agreed. I'll add host compromise playbook steps and an optional HSM/BYOK note for customers requiring stronger isolation.
devops_tony: One more ops detail — recommend we limit kms:Decrypt to expected resources via encryption context condition, e.g.,"Condition":{"StringEquals":{"kms:EncryptionContext:account_id":"<customer>"}} — reduces blast radius.
jonathan: Also include example CLI to generate data key:```aws kms generate-data-key --key-id alias/rp-cmk --key-spec AES_256 --encryption-context "service=redwood,env=prod"```
sec-bot: Audit tip: require CloudTrail encryption for KMS logs and AWS Config rule to ensure KMS key rotation is enabled where customers accept it.
maria_s: OK next actions: 1) I'll draft a KB with key policy + grant recipes, rotation webhook spec, and playbook for host compromise; 2) jonathan to add DEK cache TTL config + forced-rotation endpoint; 3) tony to prototype grant-based retry path. Assign owners and follow up in next security sync. :thumbsup:
jonathan: Will start a PR for config and add unit tests for cache invalidation.
ashley: I'll review KB for compliance language and retention options.
sre_lee: I'll add the audit event schema to the telemetry repo.
maria_s: thanks everyone — closing the thread, will post drafts here when ready.
